title: Eight-hour read-ons with 15 minutes to sign
summary: Dylan Borland tells of Eight-hour read-ons with 15 minutes to sign, about 2015-2018 at BAE Systems, and says they saw it or took part. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: Like I got my first readons were like eight hours. Uh they gave us a stack of paper like this thick with sticky notes.

plain: Dylan Borland, a former intelligence worker who says he worked through the defence company BAE Systems between about 2015 and 2018, describes being briefed into secret programmes, a step insiders call a read-on. He tells podcast host Jesse Michels that his first read-ons lasted about eight hours, with a thick stack of paper covered in sticky notes, and that he was then given only about fifteen minutes to sign. He tells it to show how heavily guarded and rushed the access to these secrets was.
